text: The sixteenth season of The Bachelorette premiered on October 13, 2020, featuring Clare Crawley, a 39-year-old hairstylist from Sacramento, California, and Tayshia Adams, a 29-year-old phlebotomist from Corona del Mar, California. The season was originally scheduled to premiere on May 18, 2020, but was postponed indefinitely due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Filming began in early July 2020 at La Quinta Resort & Club in La Quinta, California, after being halted in March 2020 when production was suspended due to the pandemic. The initial plan included international destinations such as Chattanooga (Tennessee), Reykjavík (Iceland), Rome (Italy), and Hvar (Croatia), but these were canceled due to the worsening outbreak, and all dates were restricted to the United States. The season aired on Tuesday nights instead of its usual Monday night timeslot. Clare Crawley, who was the runner-up on the 18th season of The Bachelor with Juan Pablo Galavis and had previously appeared on seasons one and two of Bachelor in Paradise and Bachelor Winter Games, was named the Bachelorette on Good Morning America on March 2, 2020. At 39, she became the oldest Bachelorette in the show's history, surpassing Rachel Lindsay, who was 32. Crawley departed the show in episode 4 after choosing 31-year-old Dale Moss as her fiancé, making him the first African American winner in the franchise's history. The couple broke up on January 19, 2021, got back together shortly after, and ultimately separated for good on September 27, 2021. Tayshia Adams, who finished third on the 23rd season of The Bachelor with Colton Underwood and had appeared on season 6 of Bachelor in Paradise, replaced Crawley as the Bachelorette. Adams accepted a proposal from 36-year-old addiction specialist Zac Clark, concluding the season on December 22, 2020, though they ended their engagement on November 22, 2021. The season began with Crawley preparing for the role in March 2020 before production halted. After quarantine and testing, she met 31 men at La Quinta Resort & Club. Notable contestants included football players Dale Moss, Jason Foster, and Uzoma Nwachukwu, and Tyler Smith, brother of country music singer Granger Smith. Originally, 32 potential contestants were revealed on March 11, 2020, with an updated list of 42 released on July 15, 2020, including 17 from the original group. Four of the original 32 were recast: Matt James took over as the lead for season 25 of The Bachelor, becoming the first male African American lead; Greg Grippo and Karl Smith were recast for the following season; and James Clarke was recast for season 19. The final cast of 31 men was announced on September 29, 2020, and four new contestants joined in episode 5, bringing the total to 35. Due to the pandemic, the typical Men Tell All and After the Final Rose special did not occur. A group date in week 2 involved 10 men playing strip dodgeball, with each round requiring the removal of a clothing layer, which drew widespread criticism and accusations of a double standard, with fans and alumni arguing that such a date would be unacceptable if applied to women. Contestant Yosef Aborady stated he would not have participated due to concerns about his daughter seeing such content, and he was later sent home after an argument with Crawley. The season marked the first time since the second season of The Bachelorette in 2004 that dates were held entirely within the U.S., and it was the first season since 2008 not to premiere in May. Adams was named interim host for seasons 17 and 18 alongside Kaitlyn Bristowe, replacing Chris Harrison. Blake Moynes returned for season 7 and 9 of Bachelor in Paradise, quitting in week 4 of season 9, and Dale Moss returned for season 10 of Bachelor in Paradise, where he was eliminated in the finale while in a relationship with Kat Izzo. Crawley appeared on the first season of the Hulu show Got to Get Out, and Adams appeared on the first season of The Goat.
